document.title: A/S Raphel's October 4 Meeting with Assef Ali on Afghanistan (State 243042)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Pakistan: "The Taliban's Godfather"?
document.note: [Confidential] Pakistan Foreign Minister Assef Ali tells Assistant Secretary Robin Raphel that Pakistan's message to the Rabbani opposition was to unite against Kabul but not attack it. He does not deny significant Pakistani contact with and some support for the Taliban, saying little outside material support was needed given their Pashtun support.

events.description: Raphel met informally with Assef Ali after his meeting with Perry
Taliban captured Herat from Ismael Khan
Assef Ali met Secretary of Defense Perry.
Raphel met Assef Ali, Lodhi and Brig. Javed to discuss Afghanistan and Kashmir hostages.
Taliban took Herat from Ismael Khan after Dostam opened a front in Badghis and Ismael Khan's forces attempted to loot Gereshk.
Taliban captured a Russian plane carrying 32 tons of ammunition bound for Kabul, cutting the airbridge.
Rabbani promised Mestiri he would resign.
State Department cable 243042 reporting the meeting was sent.

key_claims: Assef Ali blamed Ismael Khan's mistakes and Kabul's use of Panjshiri Tajiks, not Pakistan, for Herat's fall.
Ali conceded Pakistan had significant contact with and gave some support to the Taliban.
Ali claimed Taliban funding came mainly from Kandahari traders and that Pashtun support made outside aid unnecessary.
Pakistan has contacts with all major opponents of Rabbani and Masood and encourages their cooperation, but cautioned against attacking Kabul.
Ali said Iran was frenzied over Herat's fall and might do something physical.
US policy was to back the UN Special Mission and not endorse any Afghan faction.
